name: Accounting
description: Financial accounting for senior secondary: principles, books of original entry, ledger, control accounts, adjustments and final accounts, aligned to the WAEC/NECO Financial Accounting and JAMB syllabuses.

topics.name: Introduction to Accounting
topics.summary: What accounting is for, the principles that govern it, and the documents that start every record.

subtopics.name: Meaning and Principles
subtopics.summary: Users of accounting information and the concepts that keep the books honest.

objectives.text: Define accounting and distinguish it from bookkeeping
List internal and external users of accounting information
State the business-entity, going-concern, matching, prudence and consistency concepts

subtopics.name: Source Documents
subtopics.summary: Invoices, receipts, credit notes, debit notes and how each starts an entry.

objectives.text: Name the common source documents and the transaction each records
Distinguish an invoice from a credit note and a debit note
Trace a source document into the correct book of original entry

subtopics.name: The Accounting Equation
subtopics.summary: Assets = Capital + Liabilities, and how every transaction keeps it in balance.

objectives.text: State the accounting equation and define asset, liability and capital
Show the effect of a transaction on the equation
Classify items as assets, liabilities, income or expenses

topics.name: Double Entry and the Ledger
topics.summary: Every debit has a credit. The ledger is where those entries live.

subtopics.name: The Double-Entry Principle
subtopics.summary: Debit the receiver, credit the giver — applied to cash, goods and expenses.

objectives.text: State the double-entry rule for assets, liabilities, income and expenses
Record a simple transaction as a debit and a matching credit
Explain why the trial balance agrees when double entry is complete

subtopics.name: Ledger Accounts
subtopics.summary: T-accounts, balancing, and the personal, real and nominal classification.

objectives.text: Open and post to a T-account
Balance a ledger account and bring down the balance
Classify accounts as personal, real or nominal

subtopics.name: The Trial Balance
subtopics.summary: Listing debit and credit balances to test the arithmetic of the ledger.

objectives.text: Extract a trial balance from a set of ledger balances
State errors that a trial balance will not reveal
Explain what an imbalance means and the first checks to make

topics.name: Books of Original Entry
topics.summary: Journals and cash books that feed the ledger.

subtopics.name: The Journals
subtopics.summary: Sales, purchases, returns and the general journal.

objectives.text: State the use of the sales, purchases, returns inwards and returns outwards journals
Record a transaction in the appropriate journal
Explain when the general journal is used, including opening entries

subtopics.name: The Cash Book
subtopics.summary: Two- and three-column cash books, and cash versus bank columns.

objectives.text: Record receipts and payments in a two-column cash book
Use the discount columns of a three-column cash book
Treat a contra entry between cash and bank

subtopics.name: Petty Cash and the Imprest System
subtopics.summary: A float for small payments, restored at the end of each period.

objectives.text: Explain the imprest system of petty cash
Record petty-cash payments and the reimbursement that restores the float
Analyse petty-cash payments into expense columns

topics.name: Control Accounts and Errors
topics.summary: Checking the debtors and creditors ledgers, and putting mistakes right.

subtopics.name: Control Accounts
subtopics.summary: Sales-ledger and purchases-ledger control accounts as a check on personal ledgers.

objectives.text: State the purpose of sales-ledger and purchases-ledger control accounts
Prepare a sales-ledger control account from given totals
Interpret a debit balance in the purchases ledger or a credit balance in the sales ledger

subtopics.name: Bank Reconciliation
subtopics.summary: Why the cash-book bank balance differs from the bank statement, and how to agree them.

objectives.text: List items that cause the cash book and bank statement to differ
Update the cash book for bank charges, standing orders and direct credits
Prepare a bank reconciliation statement

subtopics.name: Errors and the Suspense Account
subtopics.summary: Errors of principle, omission, commission and the suspense account that holds a difference.

objectives.text: Classify errors that do and do not affect the trial-balance agreement
Correct errors using journal entries
Use a suspense account to hold and then clear a trial-balance difference

topics.name: Year-End Adjustments
topics.summary: Accruals, prepayments, depreciation and irrecoverable debts before final accounts.

subtopics.name: Accruals and Prepayments
subtopics.summary: Matching income and expenses to the period they belong to.

objectives.text: Define an accrual and a prepayment
Adjust expenses and income for amounts owing or paid in advance
Show accruals and prepayments in the balance sheet

subtopics.name: Depreciation
subtopics.summary: Straight-line and reducing-balance methods, and the ledger entries.

objectives.text: Explain why non-current assets are depreciated
Calculate depreciation using the straight-line and reducing-balance methods
Record depreciation in the ledger and on the balance sheet

subtopics.name: Bad and Doubtful Debts
subtopics.summary: Writing off debts that will not be paid, and providing for those that might not.

objectives.text: Distinguish a bad debt from a provision for doubtful debts
Record the write-off of a bad debt
Account for an increase or decrease in the provision

topics.name: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
topics.summary: Trading account, profit and loss account, and the statement of financial position.

subtopics.name: The Trading Account
subtopics.summary: Finding gross profit from sales, purchases and inventories.

objectives.text: Prepare a trading account and calculate cost of sales
Treat carriage inwards, returns and closing inventory
Interpret a fall or rise in the gross-profit margin

subtopics.name: The Profit and Loss Account
subtopics.summary: From gross profit to net profit after operating expenses.

objectives.text: Prepare a profit and loss account from a trial balance and adjustments
Distinguish capital expenditure from revenue expenditure
Explain the effect of an omitted accrual on net profit

subtopics.name: The Balance Sheet
subtopics.summary: A classified statement of financial position after the profit and loss account.

objectives.text: Prepare a classified balance sheet from closing ledger balances
Show capital, net profit and drawings in the capital section
Distinguish current from non-current assets and liabilities

topics.name: Partnerships and Incomplete Records
topics.summary: When there is more than one owner, or the books are incomplete.

subtopics.name: Partnership Accounts
subtopics.summary: Appropriation of profit, current accounts, and the partnership agreement.

objectives.text: State the provisions of the Partnership Act when there is no agreement
Prepare an appropriation account for interest on capital, salaries and share of profit
Show partners' current and capital accounts

subtopics.name: Incomplete Records
subtopics.summary: Building a statement of affairs and finding profit when double entry was never kept.

objectives.text: Prepare opening and closing statements of affairs
Calculate profit as closing capital + drawings − additional capital − opening capital
Reconstruct a sales or purchases figure from control-account logic

subtopics.name: Not-for-Profit Organisations
subtopics.summary: Receipts and payments, income and expenditure, and the accumulated fund.

objectives.text: Distinguish a receipts-and-payments account from an income-and-expenditure account
Calculate the accumulated fund
Treat subscriptions in arrears and in advance

topics.name: Interpretation of Accounts
topics.summary: Ratios that turn a set of final accounts into a story about the business.

subtopics.name: Accounting Ratios
subtopics.summary: Profitability, liquidity and efficiency ratios a WAEC candidate is expected to compute.

objectives.text: Calculate gross-profit margin, net-profit margin and return on capital employed
Calculate current ratio and acid-test ratio
Interpret a change in a ratio in plain language

subtopics.name: Manufacturing Accounts
subtopics.summary: Prime cost, factory overheads and the transfer to the trading account.

objectives.text: Prepare a manufacturing account and identify prime cost
Treat factory overheads and work in progress
Explain why a manufacturer needs a manufacturing account as well as a trading account

subtopics.name: Departmental Accounts
subtopics.summary: Splitting profit by department so management can see which section earns.

objectives.text: State reasons for keeping departmental accounts
Apportion expenses between departments on a given basis
Prepare a departmental trading and profit and loss account
